testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: rebase-check job (pull_request-only branch-currency assertion, not meaningful in a worktree of origin/main); proc-macos job (node --test tests/proc.test.mjs on macOS) (subsumed by the full suite on this macOS host); smoke-omp job (needs pinned omp installed via bun, absent here); install-and-smoke job (needs pinned omp installed via bun and network, absent here).

unverified.claim: The § 5.1 note (lines 207-211) and the § 5.2 note (lines 245-249) say that with no Fit read the view's source line reads 'starting table · no Fit yet: the next phase 0 writes one'. That holds only for a missing Fit. An unreadable or invalid Fit, which is also a case where no Fit is read, reads 'starting table · the Fit is not read: <why>'.
unverified.evidence: Ran `node probe-source.mjs` in correctness/, calling computeCellEvidence from the copy with the starting table and guard null. It printed: {"status":"missing"} => "starting table · no Fit yet: the next phase 0 writes one"; {"status":"unreadable","why":"not JSON"} => "starting table · the Fit is not read: not JSON". The code is compute-cell-evidence.mjs:459, `fit?.status === "unreadable" ? `the Fit is not read: ${fit.why}` : "no Fit yet: …"`.
unverified.suggested_fix: In both notes, name the second wording: "no Fit yet: the next phase 0 writes one" when there is no Fit file, and "the Fit is not read: <why>" when the file cannot be read or is invalid.

unverified.claim: The tier-routing note says the Fit is 'recomputed at every phase 0', and the router spec R5 cadence note (line 774) says metrics-refresh 'computes the Fit at every phase 0'. In the code the Fit runs only after the guard duty wrote a guard; otherwise phase 0 prints 'fit: skipped, no guard written' and leaves the old file.
unverified.evidence: Read metrics-refresh.mjs:335-336 (`if (written === null) return say(`fit: skipped, no guard written — ${FIT} left as it is`)`), :360-371 (`written` is set only when the costGuard duty returns, and `fit(repo, written)` is called only without --no-fit), and the header at :64 ('After the cost guard wrote a guard, and only then'). This was read, not executed.
unverified.suggested_fix: Change 'recomputed at every phase 0' to 'recomputed at each phase 0 that writes a cost guard', or similar wording, in both notes.

unverified.claim: The R6 #3895 paragraph still says `route` calls rowDispatch for 'its policy row, its base row (the policy row's own unless arm B sizes it) and its draw', and the #4247 note under it does not cover that sentence. In the landed route, rowDispatch is called for the run's Objective and for `cost` (the draw centre), and no arm B sizing ever changes a base row.
unverified.evidence: Read ticket-router.mjs:612-614 (`const dispatch = (o) => rowDispatch({ table, guard, objective: o, stratum, install }); const policyRow = dispatch(objective); const drawRow = dispatch("cost");`) and :576-578 ('A live B Pull records its sizing verdict and routes as an A Pull does'). The #4247 note at the end of that paragraph covers only `install` and `draw.cells`. This was read, not executed.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add a clause to that #4247 note: route calls rowDispatch for the Objective's row and for the `cost` row its draw is centred on, and arm B no longer sizes a base row (R2's note).

unverified.claim: The notes say the Fit is computed/recomputed 'at every phase 0', but metrics-refresh only runs the Fit after the cost guard wrote a guard, so a phase 0 with no guard writes no Fit; the note on line ~230 and tier-routing.md line 11 overstate it.
unverified.evidence: plugin/scripts/metrics-refresh.mjs:64-65: 'After the cost guard wrote a guard, and only then, the Router's fit … runs in-process'. Notes at pr.diff lines 11-12 ('recomputed at every phase 0') and 230-231 ('computes the Fit at every phase 0'); cockpit-tabs note elsewhere correctly says 'at phase 0 only'.
unverified.suggested_fix: Say 'at each phase 0 that has a cost guard' (or 'at phase 0 after the guard writes') in the two notes.

unverified.claim: Note cites § 2.12 of the new spec for `assignment_prob`, but § 2.12 item 4 only says 'assignment probability' (the column name `assignment_prob` appears only in code), so the cited section does not name that identifier.
unverified.evidence: grep assignment_prob in docs/specs/2026-11-01-self-refining-router-design.md: no hits; § 2.12 item 4 (line 191) reads 'assignment probability'; identifier exists at plugin/scripts/ticket-router.mjs:581,644.
unverified.suggested_fix: Acceptable as is; optionally drop the identifier or cite ticket-router.mjs.
